question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the technologies from the left onto the correct descriptions on the right.
targets: authenticates clients and servers in NFSv4
authenticates clients to corporate directory systems
theory: NFSv2/v3 traditionally trust whichever machine sends the RPC request (AUTH_SYS), effectively authenticating the client machine rather than the individual user; NFSv4 raised the bar by supporting strong, user-level authentication, typically delivered through Kerberos, which itself provides mutual, ticket-based authentication between clients and servers. RADIUS, in contrast, is a general AAA protocol commonly used to authenticate clients against a centralized corporate directory rather than being an NFS-specific mechanism - understanding which authentication model each protocol/version relies on is the concept being tested. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 10 - NFS Concepts)
